The other recension has ཡུད་ཙམ་རེ་སེ་གོལ་རེའི་ཡུན. Possible readings: ཡུད་པ་རེ་སེ་གོལ (taken) or ཡུད་པ་རེས་གོལ (unlikely, because སེ carries its own e).

## Other observations (no change to the witness text)

- 19.1 (filler dots): after ཡུན་རིང་ the print has a short row of filler dots (three or four tsheg-like dots, ··· ) before གནས་པ, as space-filler in the line. They are not letters, so I left them out of the text. If the house rule wants them, they belong at རིང་··· གནས.
- 18.2 དྷུ་ཏི: no a-chung can be seen under the dh-stack here. At 18.4, ཨཱ་ཝ་དྷཱུ་ཏིར shows a separate a-chung hook under ཨ (loop on the left, tail to the right, unlike the zhabs-kyu ུ) and under དྷ. Both read as the witness has them. This print's habit of sometimes writing length marks and sometimes not matches the p. 16 note.
- 18.5 ཀྱིས: a second, lower dot follows the tsheg (it looks like ":"). I take it as an ink speck, not a visarga.
- 19.5 (line end): after དེས་ there is a stray small mark near the frame. It is not a letter.
- Tshegs in this scan often merge into the head-line (for example in རྩ་རྦ་རླབས་). Where I couldn't see one, I kept the witness's tsheg, except where a clear gap shows none (18.4 མཆད, 20.5 ནམཁའ).

## The page 19 → 20 join (question from the coordinator)

On the images the print really does run this way, and no line has been dropped. p. 19 (n20) has exactly five lines, and line 5 ends at the frame with …གཅིག་རྩར་བཞག་ཏེ༔ དེས་. p. 20 (n21, margin number 20, following 19 on n20) line 1 begins ད་ནི་ས་ཆུ་ལ་ཐིམ་པའི་རྟགས་གདའོ༔ ཞེས་རྟགས་རྣམས་རིམ་བ་ལྟར་གསལ་བཏབ་ལ༔.
The apparent jump came from the witness's typo ད་དི for ད་ནི. Read correctly, it says: "…set beside [the dying person] a close friend; he [says]: 'Now the sign of earth dissolving into water is here.' In this way the signs are made clear one after another…" The text cites only the first dissolution sign and covers the rest with ཞེས་…རིམ་བ་ལྟར. The other recension runs the same way: …གཅིག་རྩར་བཞག་སྟེ༔ ད་ནི་ས་ཆུར་ཐིམ་པའི་རྟགས་གདབ་པོ༔ ཞེས་རྣམས་རིམ་པ་ལྟར་གསལ་གདབ་ལ༔.

## Suspected misprints (kept as printed)

1. 18.4 ནང་དབུགས་མཆད་ཀྱི་བར་དེར, probably meant as མ་ཆད ("before the inner breath has stopped"). Certainty is high on the sense: the sentence contrasts ཕྱི་དབུགས་ཆད with an inner breath not yet stopped, and the other recension has མ་ཆད་པའི. The print shows no tsheg between མ and ཆ, so this is either a dropped tsheg or a misprint. A `# fix: མཆད => མ་ཆད` is reasonable.
2. 18.1 རྩ་རྦ་རླབས་རྩིར་བ: the letters are certain (the same ra-mgo + ཙ shape as the preceding རྩ). Probably meant as བཙིར ("press, squeeze"), which the other recension has. Certainty is moderate: རྩིར is not a known verb form. It could be a misprint, or a spelling variant for gtsir/btsir.
3. Not misprints, the print's own spelling: 19.2 སྐྱར for བསྐྱར ("repeat", the other recension has བསྐྱར); 20.1 རིམ་བ for རིམ་པ (the letter is the closed བ; compare the print's habit with ཞུས་བ); 20.5 ནམཁའ (contraction).

## Where the other recension differs in sense (print followed)

- 18.2: print རླུང་དྷུ་ཏི་ནས་ཕྱིར་ལོག་སྟེ་ཚངས་བུག་གི་ལམ་དུ་ཐོན་ངེས་སོ ("the wind turns back out of the dhūtī and certainly goes out by the path of the Brahma-aperture"). Other recension རླུང་དྷུ་ཏིར་ཚུད་ནས་ཕྱིར་ལོག་མི་ཤེས་ཏེ ("the wind, having entered the dhūtī, cannot turn back"). This is the opposite statement about turning back.
- 18.3: print ངོ་སྤྲོད་ཀྱང་འདིའི་དུས་སུ… / འདིའི་དུས་སུ; other recension དེའི. Little difference in sense.
- 18.4: print ཐིམ་པའི་བར་ཡིན་ ("the interval when…"); other recension ཐིམ་པའི་དུས་ཡིན་ ("the time when…"). Little difference.
- 18.5: print ཤེས་པ་བརྒྱལ; other recension རྣམ་ཤེས་བརྒྱལ. Same sense.
- 19.3: print ལ་ལ་ཟན་ཟ་ཡུན་རེ་གནས་པ་ཡོད ("some remain for about the time of eating a meal"); other recension ལ་ལ་ཟན་ཟ་ཡུན་ཙམ་ལས་མི་གནས་པ་ཡང་ཡོད་དེ ("some do not remain longer than a meal's time"). One gives a duration, the other an upper limit.
- 19.3: print མདོ་རྒྱུད་ཕལ་ཆེར་ན (locative); other recension ལས. Same sense.
- 20.4: print འཆི་བ་དེ་འོང་བར་འདུག་གིས ("that death seems about to come"); other recension འཆི་བ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་དེ་འོངས་ནས་འདུག་པས ("what is called death has come"). The print puts death as imminent, the other recension as already arrived.
- 20.5: print བྱམས་པ་དང་སྙིང་རྗེ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་བསྒོམ་པ་འབའ་ཞིག་གིས; other recension བྱམས་སྙིང་རྗེ་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་སེམས་འབའ་ཞིག་གིས. The print adds "meditating on" (བསྒོམ་པ).

| 26.5 | དགོ་སོ༔ | དགོསོ༔ | ×6 + pixel check: naro over ག and over ས, with no room for a tsheg between them. One ས serves both syllables (contraction of དགོས་སོ, cf. ནམཁའི in read2_B) |
| 27.1 | ༔དག་པོ་ཐེ་བས་ན | ༔དང་པོ་ཐེབས་ན | ×5: ང, and ཐེབས is one syllable with no tsheg inside it |
| 27.1 | གཉིས་པལ་གསལ | གཉིས་པར་གསལ | ར, not ལ |

Kept from the witness after checking: 24.1 རིགས་པ (ས clearly printed), 25.1 ཟེར (ཟ, not ཞ), 25.3 སླེབ་བའི
(both letters are བ-shaped; the other recension has པའི), 25.5 ཀློགས་ཏེ, 26.1 སྒོཾས (see below), 27.1 གདབ་བས.

## Ligatures and abbreviations (as printed; candidates for `# fix:`)

- **-གས ligature** (25.3 འཇིགས, 26.5 རིགས): the print has one glyph for the final -gs. It looks like a ཌ with a
  hook, and the witness types it as ཌ. Unicode has no character for it, so read2_C.txt writes the letters it stands
  for (གས). No fix needed, but the drafter may want to note it once. Elsewhere on these pages (25.5 རིགས, 26.4 རིགས,
  26.5 ཉམས etc.) -གས is written out in full.
- **26.1 སྒོཾས** for སྒོམས: a mid-line abbreviation, a small circle (ཾ) above the naro in place of མ. It is kept as
  printed. Fix: `# fix: སྒོཾས => སྒོམས`. The same line spells སྒོམས out in full once.
- **26.1 ཅནྡུ[?]** for ཅན་དུ, a contraction (see [?]). Fix: `# fix: ཅནྡུ => ཅན་དུ` (the [?] goes when the line is settled).
- **26.3 འདེབྶ** (line end) for འདེབས, with ས subjoined to བ. Fix: `# fix: འདེབྶ => འདེབས`.
- **26.5 དགོསོ** for དགོས་སོ (contraction). Fix: `# fix: དགོསོ => དགོས་སོ`.
- **Line joins with no tsheg:** 24.4/24.5 འོང|ངོ༔ (`# fix: འོངངོ => འོང་ངོ`), 26.1/26.2 ཡིན|ན (`# fix: ཡིནན => ཡིན་ན`),
  26.2/26.3 གསོན|བོའི (`# fix: གསོནབོའི => གསོན་བོའི`).

## [?]

- **26.1 ཅནྡུ[?]**: after བཅས་ཅ the print has one stacked glyph with a zhabkyu, not two syllables. At ×9 the top
  letter has ན's left loop and stem, and below it a second letter ending in the ུ hook. I read it as ནྡུ, a contraction
  of ཅན་དུ, the witness's reading. The sense is certain (གདོས་བཅས་ཅན་དུ་མ་སྒོམས). The exact subscript (ད or ཏ) and
  whether it is ན at all are not certain at this resolution.

## Suspected misprints (print kept in read2_C.txt)

- **25.2 དུ་རྒོད་ཀྱང་ཐོས་སོ** → most likely **ངུ་རྒོད** ("weeping and laughing", rgod = dgod "laugh"). The other
  recension has ངུ་འབོད. Moderate certainty. The first letter has the full ད structure (head, stub, middle bar and a
  right descender ending in the ུ hook), like the ད of ཉེ་དུ on the same line, so I read ད, as the witness does. A
  ང cannot be wholly excluded, because the zhabkyu hides the foot of the letter. དུ gives no sense here, and ངུ fits.
  རྒོད is clear: ར-head over ག, with naro and ད.
- **26.5 སྡོམ་པ་ཤོར་བདང་༔** → **ཤོར་བ་དང**. Certain as to sense. No tsheg is visible between བ and ད, while the tsheg
  after ཤོར is visible. The witness also has བདང. Other recension: ཤོར་བ་དང.
- **24.2 གསུམ་པ་རང་གི་ཤེས་ནས** → possibly **རང་གི་ངོ་ཤེས་ནས** or **རང་ངོ་ཤེས་ནས** (other recension: གསུམ་པས་རང་ངོ་ཤེས་ནས).
  Low certainty. The print clearly has གི (a ག with gigu and a long stem, not ང). It reads "third, knowing [it as]
  one's own", which is possible but thin.
- **24.1 རིགས་པ** for རིག་པ ("awareness"). Low; probably the print's spelling habit (cf. ཤེས་རིགས in read2_B 23.5).
  The ས is clearly printed.

## Other recension: differences of sense

- 24.1 print: ཞེས་ལན་གསུམ་མམ༔ བདུན་གྱི་བར་ལ་སྒྲ་དག་ལ་ཚིག་གསལ་བར་བརྗོད ("…with clear sound and clear words"); the other
  recension lacks ཚིག.
- 24.2 print: དེས་སྐད་ཅིག་དང་པོ་བླ་མས་ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ལྟར་དྲན ("at the first instant he recalls it as the lama pointed it
  out"); other: དེས་དང་པོ་སྔར་བླ་མས་ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་དྲན ("first he recalls what the lama pointed out before"). Same point,
  different wording. The print also lacks the other recension's closing དེ་གྲོལ་ལོ after ངོ་འཕྲོད (24.3).
- 24.2 print: རང་གི་ཤེས་ནས; other: རང་ངོ་ཤེས་ནས ("recognising oneself"). See misprints.
- 24.5 print: ཤེས་པ་གསལ་ལམ་གྱིས་འོང་ངོ; other: …འོང. Same sense.
- 25.2 print: ཉེ་དུ་འབྲེལ་བ་ཡང་སྔར་བཞིན་མཐོང་ནས་ཡོད ("relatives too are seen as before"); other: …མཐོང་ནས་འོང.
  Print: དུ་རྒོད (ངུ་རྒོད "weeping and laughing") ཀྱང་ཐོས; other: ངུ་འབོད ("weeping and wailing") ཀྱང་ཐོས.
  Print: ལས་ཀྱི་འཁྲུལ་སྣང ("the karmic delusive appearances"); other: ལས་ཀྱི་རླུང་དང་འཁྲུལ་སྣང ("the karmic wind and the
  delusive appearances").
- 25.4 print: ངོ་སྤྲད་དེ་སྐྱར་ནས་གདབ ("repeat that pointing-out"); other: ངོ་སྤྲོད་དེ་ཀ་བསྐྱར་ལ་གདབ. Same sense.
- 25.5 print: ཁྱོད་རང་གི་ཡི་དམ་འདི་སྒོམས ("meditate on this yidam of yours"); other: ཁྱེད་རང་གི་ཡི་དམ་ནི་སྒོམས.
- 26.1 print: ཆུ་ཟླ་ལྟ་བུར; other: ཆུ་ནང་གི་ཟླ་བ་ལྟར. Same sense. Print: གདོས་བཅས་ཅན་དུ་མ་སྒོམས ("do not meditate
  on it as something material"); other: གདོས་བཅོས་མ་སུ་སྒོམས (corrupt or different; the print's reading is the clearer).
- 26.4 print: ནད་དྲག་པོས; other: ནད་གཅོད་དྲག་པོས. Print: གདམས་པ་འདི་ཤིན་ཏུ་དགོས / 26.5 འདི་ཅི་ནས་ཀྱང་དགོས; the other
  recension has ཅིས་ཀྱང and ཤིན་ཏུ་ནས་ཀྱང the other way round. Same sense.
- 27.1 print: བར་དོ་གཉིས་པར་གསལ་གདབ་བས༔ རིགས་སད་ནས ("the type/faculty awakens"); compare the other recension's
  wording at this point when the next part is read (not needed for this part).
